t.7.82.1: Having narrated this to his two brothers, Kākutstha of boundless splendour once again addressed to Lakṣmaṇa these words imbued with dharma.
t.7.82.2: Vasiṣṭha and Vāmadeva, Jābāli and then Kaśyapa, and all the foremost of the twice-born, with the horse sacrifice set before them as their chief concern.
t.7.82.3: Having summoned all these and taken counsel with them, O Lakṣmaṇa, I shall release with due ceremony a horse endowed with auspicious marks.
t.7.82.4: Having heard those words spoken by Rāghava, he, swift in his stride, summoned all the twice-born and brought them before Rāghava.
t.7.82.5: Seeing Rāghava, who was like a god and utterly unassailable, and who had bowed at their feet in reverence, they honored him with blessings.
t.7.82.6: Then Rāghava, having joined his palms in reverence, spoke to those best of the twice-born words that were in accord with dharma and concerned the Aśvamedha.
t.7.82.7: Then, having heard the words of those foremost of the twice-born, wondrous in their vision and concerned with the Aśvamedha, he became exceedingly pleased.
t.7.82.8: Having understood their opinion, Rāma said to Lakṣmaṇa: "O mighty-armed one, send word to the great-souled Sugrīva."
t.7.82.9: Come quickly, together with the mighty monkeys and the many who depend on them, to partake of the finest of sacrifices; may good fortune be with you.
t.7.82.11: And let the kings who wish to do what is dear to me, O tiger among men, come quickly with their followers to the unsurpassed sacrificial ground.
t.7.82.10: And let the mighty-armed Vibhīṣaṇa, swift in valor, come to the horse sacrifice, surrounded by many rākṣasas who move wherever they wish.
t.7.82.12: And those twice-born who are devoted to dharma and have gone to other lands, invite them all to the horse sacrifice, O Lakṣmaṇa.
t.7.82.13: O mighty-armed one, let the sages rich in austerity be summoned, and also those great sages who have gone to other lands, together with their wives.
t.7.82.14: And let a very great sacrificial enclosure be ordered in the Naimiṣa forest by the Gomatī, O mighty-armed one, for that place is holy and unsurpassed.
t.7.82.16: Let the wise Bharata go on ahead, placing before him many crores of gold coins and hundreds more of bullion.
t.7.82.15: Let a hundred thousand loads of fine, plump rice grains and ten thousand loads of sesame and mudga beans go on ahead, O mighty one.
t.7.82.17: The streets of shops within the market, and all the actors and dancers, the merchants, the young and the old, and the twice-born of well-composed mind.
t.7.82.18: Send along the skilled overseers of works and the highly learned artisans; and let all my mothers, as well as the inner apartments of the princes, go too.
t.7.82.19: Let the greatly wise Bharata go on ahead, placing before him my golden wife, fit for consecration in the rite of sacrifice.
